oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer JWT presented to Vault JWT auth can be reused; documentation does not describe jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT auth login docs + RFC 6750/7519 behavior
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability for stateless JWT verification.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf, or platform-specific handling of future nbf when not explicitly enforced, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag absence of nbf enforcement by itself as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC authorization codes and lookup-style artifacts are used according to their documented flow semantics; repeated reads of lookup endpoints are not themselves replay vulnerabilities unless documented single-use.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat repeated discovery/JWKS/userinfo retrieval as replay.

oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer token can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions unless explicit use limits are configured on the issued Vault token.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same valid bearer token as replay unless token_num_uses or another one-time mechanism is configured.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT not-before enforcement is configurable via not_before_leeway and may be effectively relaxed; absence of nbf is not itself a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT auth role docs + RFC 7519 §4.1.5
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf, or behavior around future nbf when not strictly configured, is not automatically a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC provider access tokens are bearer tokens and can be reused until expiry.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC provider token endpoint returns token_type Bearer
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same valid access token as replay unless the platform documents one-time semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: When an admin updates JWT/OIDC validation config such as jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, jwt_validation_pubkeys, or bound_issuer, subsequent logins are expected to use the new trust settings.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat successful login under the new admin-configured trust anchor as trust-anchor substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Request-object attacks such as alg=none request JWTs are not applicable to this endpoint.

oidc_jwt.description: Public OIDC clients must use PKCE in Vault's OIDC provider; confidential clients may use PKCE optionally.
oidc_jwt.note: A token exchange failure without code_verifier for a public client is expected behavior, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients; '*' is the explicit allow-all sentinel.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not interpret empty allowed_client_ids as wildcard or missing validation.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC client with no assignments allows no Vault entities to authenticate through the client; allow_all must be supplied to permit all entities.
oidc_jwt.note: Baseline login failures may be due to missing assignments rather than audience or scope enforcement.

oidc_jwt.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to 'any', group policies apply across namespace boundaries regardless of token namespace hierarchy.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-namespace policy application is by design in this mode and should not be flagged as escalation.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's documented OIDC provider metadata declares request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Request-object signature tests are not applicable to this provider surface.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC provider does not support request or request_uri authorization parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: Request-object signature tests are inapplicable; rejection is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, causing privilege sharing, and Vault explicitly warns operators to avoid alias reuse.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault entity alias API IMPORTANT NOTE
oidc_jwt.note: This can look like a collision bug but is a documented consequence of alias cardinality choices; baseline setups should avoid accidental alias reuse.

oidc_jwt.constraint: JWT auth config requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not send combinations, or setup is invalid and I1 tests become uninterpretable.

JWT roles require at least one bound value. The fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, bound_claims, or other documented bound values on /v1/auth/{mount}/role/{role_name}; otherwise role creation/update is invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless testing the by-design unbound case. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the iss claim, so issuer-substitution tests would pass trivially due to missing configuration rather than a validation bypass.

For I1 signing-key rotation and trust-anchor substitution tests, bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. If the fuzzer needs issuer enforcement, do NOT use jwks_pairs; use jwks_url or oidc_discovery_url instead.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple different sub values to authenticate to the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to a wildcard.

bound_audiences is exact audience membership matching against JWT aud claims. There is no companion type parameter. Wildcards are not documented. For I4 or cross-provider tests requiring multiple different audiences to pass the same role, either omit bound_audiences when the test permits or explicitly configure all accepted audience values; do NOT use '*' expecting wildcard behavior.

bound_claims matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match bound_claims entries must be omitted unless every tested identity uses the same claim value; setting a default string-mode value of '*' matches only the literal asterisk.

bound_claims accepts expected values of string, integer, boolean, or list of strings, but default bound_claims_type='string' performs literal exact matching. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default string mode so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. A scalar string claim is not valid for group alias creation. For I4 type-confusion-groups tests, distinguish rejection of wrong claim type from identity-collision behavior.

Numeric sentinel semantics on JWT leeway fields are nontrivial: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60s, not literal zero; value -1 disables added leeway. expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150s, not literal zero; value -1 disables added leeway. not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150s, not literal zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on JWT roles, include a CONTROL login with a valid token in the same setup. Because leeway defaults are nonzero when set to 0 or omitted, an attack token near the boundary may still be accepted by design. Use claims far outside the configured leeway or set the relevant leeway field to -1 for strict testing.

JWT replay with the same bearer JWT is not prevented by any documented jti tracking in Vault JWT auth. Do NOT flag replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti as I2 vulnerabilities for this platform; bearer JWT reuse is expected unless another one-time mechanism is documented.

For I3 config-change tests, new logins after modify_role_config or configure_jwt_validation are expected to use the updated configuration. A valid coherence test must show that the same JWT is rejected or accepted according to the new config, not treat admin-authorized config changes themselves as bugs.

For jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses default_role from mount config. To test default-role coherence, the fuzzer MUST omit the role parameter on login; supplying role explicitly bypasses default_role and invalidates the test.

Vault's OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include 'openid' and supports response_type=code only. Do not attempt implicit or hybrid flow variants here; use authorization_code flow only for OIDC provider tests.

Vault OIDC provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none against this provider endpoint; request JWT objects are not supported, so rejection/acceptance would not test request-object signature validation.

For OIDC provider PKCE tests, public clients MUST use PKCE: code_challenge is required at authorize and code_verifier is required at token. Confidential clients may omit PKCE. Interpret failures accordingly; missing code_verifier on a public client is expected rejection, not an identity mismatch.

For OIDC provider redirect_uri_mismatch tests, redirect_uri at the token endpoint must exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated. Any mismatch should be treated as flow rejection, not as an identity-binding result.

For OIDC provider audience-binding tests, client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request, and client assignments default to allowing NO Vault entities. To permit baseline logins, configure assignments explicitly (for example allow_all or a matching assignment) before testing audience or scope behavior.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider is exact list-membership with a special '*' sentinel meaning all clients allowed. Empty allowed_client_ids means no clients are allowed. Do not confuse empty with wildcard during I5 empty_audience/authorization tests.

OIDC provider client assignments default to no Vault entities allowed. If assignments is omitted or empty, baseline authorization through the client will fail regardless of token correctness. The fuzzer MUST configure assignments to permit the intended entity/group population before testing downstream OIDC behavior.

OIDC provider client_type and key are immutable after creation. If a test needs to switch between public/confidential behavior or change signing key, create a fresh client instead of attempting in-place modification.

OIDC provider client TTL fields have no documented disabling sentinel, but id_token_ttl should be less than the signing key's verification_ttl. When testing key rotation or token lifetime interactions, ensure verification_ttl exceeds id_token_ttl or validation behavior may be confounded by key expiry.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means use default retention of 10 versions, not literal zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion. Never assume 0 disables storage or causes immediate deletion.

For verify_read_secret on KV v2, the read path MUST include /data/ as /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} targets KV v1 semantics and will produce false 404/permission results on KV v2 mounts.

KV v2 list operations require policy on the /metadata/ path even when normal reads/writes use /data/. If the fuzzer uses listing during setup or verification, grant list capability on /v1/{engine}/metadata/{path}; otherwise failures are policy-shape issues, not auth bugs.

Session-use budget: Vault tokens can be created with num_uses limits, and token lookup-self plus secret reads each consume a use. If any setup path creates limited-use tokens for JWT/OIDC tests, minimum safe value is 2 for one verification call plus one access test, and 3 if both verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret are executed before cleanup.

Numeric sentinel semantics on token num_uses: value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Do not set num_uses=1 when the sequence includes verify_granted_identity before verify_read_secret, or the verification call will exhaust the token and cause a misleading 403 on the access test.

Identity alias names are security-sensitive in Vault. Documentation warns that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. For I4 collision tests, treat alias reuse/merge as a real risk condition, and ensure each test identity uses a unique alias source unless intentionally probing collision behavior.

External JWT/OIDC group-to-policy tests must use group aliases rather than manual membership on external groups. JWT groups_claim creates group aliases from list-of-string claim values; combine create_identity_group + create_group_alias with the auth mount accessor to model external group mapping correctly.

Group policy application can be globally configured to 'within_namespace_hierarchy' or 'any'. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests in Enterprise/multi-namespace environments, first determine /v1/sys/config/group-policy-application. Cross-namespace group policy effects are by design when mode='any'.

OIDC RP nonce handling differs by endpoint. Vault's JWT auth OIDC flow exposes auth_url and callback with nonce/state values, while Vault's OIDC provider authorize endpoint accepts optional nonce and returns it in the ID token. For replay/coherence tests, preserve and bind the exact nonce/state pair to the same flow; swapping them across sessions invalidates the test setup rather than proving a bug.

configure_jwt_validation MUST set exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. These validation sources are mutually exclusive; sending none or more than one is invalid test setup.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless jwks_pairs is used. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-mismatch tests become meaningless. Also note bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set.

For JWT role creation, at least one bound value must be set. A role with no bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims is invalid setup. Additionally, for jwt roles that receive an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching against JWT aud values; there is no wildcard/glob mode. For cross-provider or audience-mismatch tests, use concrete client IDs/audience strings. For multi-identity scenarios, audience variation must be driven by the JWT and role values directly, not by wildcard patterns.

bound_claims matching semantics are controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests, exact-match bound_claims entries that would vary across identities MUST be omitted entirely, not set to '*', unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to 'glob'.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' rather than the default 'string' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright by exact literal handling.

user_claim value must resolve to a STRING claim. If the selected claim is absent or non-string, login will fail before identity-binding tests run. For I4 tests, choose a stable string claim and only enable user_claim_json_pointer when the claim name is actually a JSON Pointer.

groups_claim value must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Sending a scalar string where Vault expects a list will fail type validation rather than exercising group alias behavior. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, ensure the JWT groups claim is an array of strings and that matching group aliases exist.
Numeric sentinel behavior: clock_skew_leeway value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 60 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables skew tolerance.

Numeric sentinel behavior: expiration_leeway value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Expired-token tests must account for this or use -1 for strict expiry enforcement.

Numeric sentinel behavior: not_before_leeway value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Future-nbf tests must account for this or use -1 for strict not-before enforcement.

Session-use budget: token_num_uses limits EVERY API call made with the issued Vault token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both a self-lookup and a protected-resource read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound verification calls are present.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack JWT. Without a successful control login, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken JWKS/issuer/role setup.
oidc_jwt.source: testing strategy from JWT auth docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, changing configure_jwt_validation to a new jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys is an admin-authorized trust-anchor change. The correct oracle is that NEW logins with the old key should fail after the change; do not flag acceptance of the new key as a vulnerability.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role only when configure_jwt_validation.default_role is set. If default_role is unset, omitting role is invalid setup rather than evidence of flow incoherence.

For I3 jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth tests, modify_role_config MUST tighten constraints (for example add bound_claims, narrow bound_audiences, or set bound_subject). Emptying bound_claims or removing restrictions broadens access and invalidates the test oracle.

Vault's OIDC auth_url/callback flow is session-bound by state, nonce, and optional client_nonce. For state-swap or callback-mixup tests, preserve the exact state and nonce pair returned in the auth_url-generated upstream flow; mismatching them is expected to fail and is not an identity confusion bug.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request + OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC callback requires state, nonce, and code, and client_nonce must match the value previously supplied to auth_url if used. The fuzzer MUST carry these values from the same start_oidc_auth event; cross-session reuse is invalid setup for coherence tests.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request + OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault's OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include 'openid', response_type='code', and redirect_uri to exactly match one of the client's configured redirect_uris. Redirect URI mismatch is expected rejection, not a security finding.

For Vault OIDC provider clients, public clients MUST use PKCE and confidential clients may use PKCE. Therefore, tests that omit code_verifier for public clients should expect failure by design; do not interpret this as identity mismatch. Conversely, configure public clients when you need mandatory PKCE enforcement.

OIDC token endpoint client authentication depends on client_type and auth method: public clients require client_id and code_verifier; confidential clients require either Authorization: Basic or client_secret in form body when using client_secret_post. Missing these is invalid setup, not a flow-binding bug.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids has special semantics: empty means NO clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. For I5 audience/authorization tests, never treat an empty list as permissive.

OIDC client assignments are deny-by-default: if assignments is empty, no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through the client. To allow all entities, explicitly use the built-in 'allow_all' assignment. Otherwise OIDC login failures may be caused by client assignment denial, not token validation.

OIDC client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, ensure the baseline control uses an exact configured URI; otherwise failures are expected configuration errors.

OIDC client_type and signing key are immutable after creation ('cannot be modified after creation'). If a test needs to change client_type or key, create a fresh client instead of calling update_application and expecting mutation.
OIDC provider UserInfo requires a Bearer ACCESS TOKEN, not an ID token. When using OIDC provider token responses, session_token must be access_token for subsequent verify_granted_identity calls.

Identity group aliases require the auth mount accessor of the external auth method. The supplied docs do not include a documented sys/auth accessor endpoint for JWT mounts, so create_group_alias cannot be executed unless the harness already knows the mount accessor out-of-band.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/group-alias + missing sys/auth docs in supplied corpus

oidc_jwt.constraint: External identity groups are populated through group aliases created from groups_claim values. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests, do not try to manually stuff JWT external memberships into internal group member_entity_ids; instead create an external group and bind it via create_group_alias to the JWT mount accessor and alias name.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive identifiers. Vault docs warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias reuse is a real risk surface; for baseline setup, ensure each test identity uses a unique alias value unless intentionally testing collisions.

Entity merge is an admin identity-management operation that can intentionally collapse principals, including alias conflicts on the same mount accessor. Do NOT use merge operations in I4 collision tests unless the test is explicitly about admin-authorized identity collapse; otherwise you create by-design collisions.

Group policy application mode can be 'within_namespace_hierarchy' or 'any'. In Enterprise, setting it to 'any' intentionally allows group policies to apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, record the current mode because cross-namespace policy reach may be by configuration, not a bug.

KV v2 sentinel behavior: engine config max_versions=0 does NOT mean keep zero versions; it means use the default of 10 versions. delete_version_after='0s' is the disable sentinel meaning no automatic timed deletion. Never assume 0 means immediate deletion or no retention.

KV v2 metadata sentinel behavior: per-key max_versions=0 means use the backend-configured max version, not zero retention. delete_version_after='0s' means no timed deletion. Tests that rely on version expiry must set explicit nonzero durations.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} would hit KV v1 semantics and produce false 404/permission results.

For KV v2 list operations, list capability is required on the /metadata/ path even if reads/writes use /data/. If a test needs secret listing, grant metadata-path list explicitly; otherwise LIST failures are expected ACL behavior.
configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not send combinations, or setup is invalid.
When jwks_pairs is configured, bound_issuer cannot be configured. Do not attempt issuer-binding tests with jwks_pairs; use jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys instead.
create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A role with no bound constraints is invalid test setup.

For jwt roles carrying an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, include a control token whose aud matches the configured bound_audiences.

user_claim must reference a claim whose value is a STRING. Do not use numeric, boolean, array, or object claims for identity binding tests, or login will fail for type reasons rather than security reasons.

groups_claim must reference a claim whose value is a LIST OF STRINGS. For group-policy escalation tests, send groups as an array of strings; a scalar string is invalid setup and may fail before alias/policy mapping is exercised.

bound_audiences is exact audience membership matching only; there is no wildcard or type-control parameter. For cross-identity or cross-provider scenarios where multiple aud values must pass, configure an explicit list of allowed audiences or omit the constraint when the test requires unrestricted audience handling.

bound_claims defaults to bound_claims_type='string', meaning values are treated as literals and must match exactly. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match claim constraints must be omitted if multiple distinct values need to authenticate; setting '*' under string mode matches only the literal asterisk.
For I5 wildcard tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type='glob'. Only in glob mode does '*' act as a wildcard; in the default string mode it is a literal character.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default string mode so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, NOT strict zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means no skew allowance.

expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, NOT strict zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. For expired-token tests, do not use 0 expecting immediate expiry enforcement.

not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, NOT strict zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. For future-token/nbf tests, do not use 0 expecting strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT auth, include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the attack token. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken role/config setup.
oidc_jwt.source: testing strategy from auth/jwt role and config docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider authorization requests require scope to include 'openid'. Omitting openid is invalid OIDC setup and will not exercise the intended flow.

OIDC provider client redirect_uris must EXACTLY match the redirect_uri used at authorize and token endpoints. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, keep the baseline exact-match control first; mismatches are expected flow rejection, not identity confusion.
Vault OIDC provider supports response_type 'code' only. Do not attempt implicit or hybrid flow variants against this endpoint.

For public OIDC clients, PKCE is required: start_oidc_auth must include code_challenge and exchange_code_for_token must include code_verifier. For confidential clients, PKCE is optional. Test PKCE behavior with the correct client_type or results are uninterpretable.

Vault's OIDC discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider authorization endpoint; request JWT objects are unsupported, so rejection is by design and acceptance tests are inapplicable.

For OIDC replay protection tests, send and verify nonce even though the authorize parameter is documented as optional. The docs strongly encourage nonce and the token response example includes it in the ID token. A valid replay test must compare behavior with matching vs missing/mismatched nonce under the same flow.
exchange_code_for_token uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded parameters. Send form-encoded bodies, not JSON, or the token request is malformed.

OIDC client_type is immutable after creation, and key is also immutable after creation. If a test needs to switch between public/confidential or signing keys, create a fresh client instead of trying to update the existing one.

OIDC client assignments default to allowing NO Vault entities. To permit authentication through a client, configure assignments explicitly, e.g. the built-in allow_all assignment or a specific assignment containing the target entity/group IDs. Otherwise auth failures are by design.
OIDC provider allowed_client_ids defaults to allowing NO clients when empty. For tests using the provider endpoints, configure allowed_client_ids explicitly or use '*'.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means keep the default 10 versions, NOT zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Never interpret these as literal zero behavior.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment: /v1/{secret-mount-path}/data/{path}. Using the mount root or KV v1 path shape will hit the wrong API and return misleading 404s.

If KV v2 cas_required is enabled at engine or metadata level, seed_protected_resource and later writes must include options.cas with the current version. Missing CAS causes write failures unrelated to authorization tests.

Vault token use budgets are consumed by EVERY API call made with that token, including verify_granted_identity via /userinfo, verify_entity_details, and verify_read_secret. If token_num_uses or num_uses is set to 1, the verification step can exhaust the token before the access test. Minimum safe value is at least 2 for one verification call plus one secret read, and higher if additional session-inspection calls are used.
oidc_jwt.source: token auth create/lookup docs and fuzzer execution context

oidc_jwt.constraint: For tests that rely on group-derived policies, create_group_alias requires the auth mount accessor and the alias name must match the external group string emitted by groups_claim. Incorrect alias names or wrong mount accessor produce false negatives in group-policy tests.

External identity alias cardinality matters: alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. For I4 collision tests, intentionally control alias names and mount accessors; for baseline setups, ensure unique alias names per principal.

Identity group policy application may be globally widened by /sys/config/group-policy-application mode='any'. For I5 group policy escalation tests in Enterprise, first confirm whether the cluster is using 'within_namespace_hierarchy' or 'any', because cross-namespace group policy application can be by configuration rather than a bug.
